comment: Every element of the reply card that comes and goes, as opposed to the frame it lives in.
reply-card.json holds the card's configuration and its footer — the divider and the
conversation hint, which every card carries from the moment it is sent to after it has
finished — and nothing else; everything a run puts on the card and takes off it again is here.
Where each one goes is decided in FeishuCardElements, which also sets the ids the run streams
into — so a deployment replacing this file is free to restyle these elements and nothing else.
'stop' is the button that cancels the run. It goes on the card as the card is created, since a
run is stoppable from the moment it is on screen, and comes off again when the run ends. It is
a button in a two-column row rather than a button, because a button placed straight in the
card body is stretched to the full width of the row on mobile, which turns cancelling a run
into the widest thing on the card. Half a row is as far as it can grow inside the first column,
and on desktop, where nothing stretches it, it stays as wide as its label. The second column is
empty on purpose: it is what reserves the other half. The element id lands on the row, not on
the button, so taking 'stop' off the card takes the whole row with it.
The rest are added the first time the run has something to put in them rather than sitting
empty on every card: an element the card carries is space the card gives up, and most runs
write no todo list and are interrupted by nobody. 'message' is the answer itself — until the
model says its first word there is nothing to show, and a streaming card says as much for
itself in the chat list. 'queued' holds what the user said
while the run was working, one quoted line per message, and goes above the answer so the card
reads in the order things were said: the message Feishu quotes above the card, then this, then
the reply. 'reasoning' is what the model thought its way through, on an endpoint that reports
it, in a panel of its own between the queued messages and the answer: it is not the answer,
so it is never folded into one. It is added the moment there is thinking to put in it and so
arrives open, because thinking is the only thing happening at that moment and a reader
watching a card do nothing is owed the one thing it is doing. It is folded away again once the
run ends and there is an answer above it to read instead — 'expanded' here is the state it is
born in, not the state it keeps. Once only, and at that one moment: Feishu reports a panel's
chevron to nobody, so anything more often would be overruling a reader's own choice over and
over rather than once, as the thing they were watching stops.
Its first nested element is the one the run streams the thinking into, which is why a
deployment restyling this panel has to keep something there to write to.
It has no border and no padding, unlike a subagent's panel: a subagent is a piece of work with
a beginning and an end, worth drawing a box around, and this is a line the reader opens. So it
reads as the card's own text with a chevron beside it — 'auto_when_fold' is what keeps the
closed line as narrow as its title while the thinking, once opened, still gets the whole width
to wrap in, and 'follow_text' is what puts the chevron beside the title rather than off at the
right edge of a row nothing else fills. The chevron points right while the pane is closed and
turns to point down as it opens, which is what the 90 degrees is: the angle is what the icon is
rotated by when expanded, not the angle it ends at, so an arrow that already points down would
want -180 and this one wants a quarter turn.
'todo' is the run's task list, under the answer. 'usage' is what the turn has cost,
in the card's footer. This key is ignored.
